title: Thermal response of single species and interaction between Gymnodinium impudicum and Heterocapsa pygmaea: Implications for harmful algal bloom dynamics.
abstract: Driven by climate change, rising seawater temperatures are expected to alter the physiology and competitive dynamics of harmful algal bloom (HAB) species. However, how warming differentially affects coexisting dinoflagellates and whether such species-specific responses translate into altered interspecific interactions remain unclear. In this study, we examined the effects of rising seawater temperatures (20, 24, and 28°C) on the physiological responses and interspecific interactions of the harmful dinoflagellates Gymnodinium impudicum and Heterocapsa pygmaea.
